The Treaty of Tordesillas was signed to resolve territorial disputes between Spain and Portugal over newly discovered lands across the ocean.  
The ability to navigate the open sea and determine direction reliably was essential for exploration and for establishing a longitudinal division of the world.  
The compass made such long-distance ocean voyages possible by providing a consistent means of orientation away from land.  
While gunpowder weapons and steel were important for conquest, they did not directly cause the need for the treaty. Germ theory is unrelated to this 1494 context.
